scenes.visual: Title card: One Tube, Bent Once.

scenes.tts: Your brain has a great many named parts. Is one shape behind them all?
scenes.visual: A side view of the adult brain covered in dozens of small grey labels. The labels fade, leaving a question mark.
scenes.narration: Your brain has a great many named parts. Is one shape behind them all?

scenes.tts: Most neurons and most glia of your brain and spinal cord come from the wall of one tube. It forms along the embryo's back.
scenes.visual: A flat sheet along an embryo's back folds up and closes into a tube. Label: open ends closed about 4 weeks after fertilization (about 6 weeks of pregnancy).
scenes.narration: Most neurons and most glia of your brain and spinal cord come from the wall of one tube. It forms along the embryo's back.

scenes.tts: The one idea: picture the central nervous system as one hollow tube, bent once.
scenes.visual: The tube glows. On-screen card: a working picture, one hollow tube, bent once.
scenes.narration: The one idea: picture the central nervous system as one hollow tube, bent once.

scenes.tts: Its walls became the brain's parts and the spinal cord. Its canal became the ventricles.
scenes.visual: The tube's wall is shaded tan, its canal blue. Labels: walls = brain parts and spinal cord; canal = ventricles.
scenes.narration: Its walls became the brain's parts and the spinal cord. Its canal became the ventricles.

scenes.tts: And the tube's own long axis, not the body's, sets what the direction words mean.
scenes.visual: An arrow runs along the centre of the tube. Labels: dorsal, ventral, rostral, caudal attach to it.
scenes.narration: And the tube's own long axis, not the body's, sets what the direction words mean.

scenes.tts: As it grows, the front end swells into three bulges: forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.
scenes.visual: The front of the tube balloons into three colour-coded bulges: forebrain (purple), midbrain (green), hindbrain (orange).
scenes.narration: As it grows, the front end swells into three bulges: forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain.

scenes.tts: The forebrain and the hindbrain each divide in two. The rest becomes the spinal cord.
scenes.visual: The purple and orange bulges each split in two, giving five; the long tail is labelled spinal cord. Colours stay fixed from here on.
scenes.narration: The forebrain and the hindbrain each divide in two. The rest becomes the spinal cord.

scenes.tts: The front of the forebrain buds out on each side, as the two cerebral hemispheres. Their canals become the two lateral ventricles.
scenes.visual: Morph toward the adult brain seen from the side. The front purple part buds out on both sides into the two hemispheres; a blue cavity glows inside each, labelled lateral ventricles, and both stay connected to the midline cavity behind them.
scenes.narration: The front of the forebrain buds out on each side, as the two cerebral hemispheres. Their canals become the two lateral ventricles.

scenes.tts: The back of the forebrain becomes the thalamus and hypothalamus, around the third ventricle.
scenes.visual: The rear purple part becomes the diencephalon, labelled thalamus and hypothalamus; a thin blue cavity glows, labelled third ventricle.
scenes.narration: The back of the forebrain becomes the thalamus and hypothalamus, around the third ventricle.

scenes.tts: The midbrain keeps a narrow canal, the cerebral aqueduct.
scenes.visual: The green midbrain; a thin blue channel through it, labelled cerebral aqueduct.
scenes.narration: The midbrain keeps a narrow canal, the cerebral aqueduct.

scenes.tts: The hindbrain becomes the pons and medulla, around the fourth ventricle.
scenes.visual: The orange parts become the pons and medulla; a tent-shaped blue cavity glows, labelled fourth ventricle.
scenes.narration: The hindbrain becomes the pons and medulla, around the fourth ventricle.

scenes.tts: The cerebellum grows from the hindbrain's dorsal side, so the fourth ventricle lies beneath it.
scenes.visual: The cerebellum grows out from the dorsal side of the orange hindbrain; the fourth ventricle lights up beneath it. Label: cerebellum over the fourth ventricle.
scenes.narration: The cerebellum grows from the hindbrain's dorsal side, so the fourth ventricle lies beneath it.

scenes.tts: In the spinal cord, many neurons that receive sensory signals develop in the tube's dorsal half, and motor neurons in its ventral half. It is a plan, not a complete split: sensory fibres also reach ventral neurons.
scenes.visual: A cross-section of the embryonic spinal cord. In the tube's wall, a dorsal zone of developing neurons is tinted blue, labelled receives sensory signals; a ventral zone is tinted red, labelled motor neurons. The rest stays grey.
scenes.narration: In the spinal cord, many neurons that receive sensory signals develop in the tube's dorsal half, and motor neurons in its ventral half. It is a plan, not a complete split: sensory fibres also reach ventral neurons.

scenes.tts: So sensory fibres enter through dorsal roots, and motor axons leave through ventral roots.
scenes.visual: A blue fibre enters at the back through a dorsal root with its ganglion; a red axon leaves at the front through a ventral root.
scenes.narration: So sensory fibres enter through dorsal roots, and motor axons leave through ventral roots.

scenes.tts: The brainstem keeps this plan, with sensory nuclei moved to the side. The forebrain does not follow it.
scenes.visual: A brainstem section opened around the fourth ventricle: blue sensory columns lie lateral, red motor columns medial, with a check mark. The forebrain gets a cross. Label: a plan for where neurons develop.
scenes.narration: The brainstem keeps this plan, with sensory nuclei moved to the side. The forebrain does not follow it.

scenes.tts: In a rat, the tube runs nearly straight from nose to tail. Dorsal is toward its back.
scenes.visual: A rat outline on all fours with a straight tube inside. Arrows: dorsal up toward its back, ventral down, rostral toward the nose, caudal toward the tail.
scenes.narration: In a rat, the tube runs nearly straight from nose to tail. Dorsal is toward its back.

scenes.tts: Stand the rat up, face pointing forward. The body, cord and brainstem turn. Only the forebrain keeps its frame.
scenes.visual: The rat rises onto its hind legs and morphs into a human silhouette. The arrows of the cord and brainstem rotate with the body; only the forebrain's arrows stay put.
scenes.narration: Stand the rat up, face pointing forward. The body, cord and brainstem turn. Only the forebrain keeps its frame.

scenes.tts: In a human, the tube bends by roughly a right angle where the midbrain meets the diencephalon. The embryo bends in three places. This one matters for naming.
scenes.visual: The bend glows at the midbrain. Label: roughly a right angle. Small inset: the embryo's three bends, this one highlighted.
scenes.narration: In a human, the tube bends by roughly a right angle where the midbrain meets the diencephalon. The embryo bends in three places. This one matters for naming.

scenes.tts: You are standing. In your spinal cord, which way does dorsal point?
scenes.visual: A standing human silhouette with the bent tube inside. A question mark beside the spinal cord.
scenes.narration: You are standing. In your spinal cord, which way does dorsal point?

scenes.tts: Toward your back. The brainstem uses the same frame. In your forebrain, dorsal points to the top of your head.
scenes.visual: Dorsal arrows appear: backward from the cord and brainstem, upward from the forebrain.
scenes.narration: Toward your back. The brainstem uses the same frame. In your forebrain, dorsal points to the top of your head.

scenes.tts: Three planes name the sections: sagittal, coronal and horizontal.
scenes.visual: Three knife planes pass through the brain in turn, each labelled with what it separates: sagittal, left from right; coronal, front from back; horizontal, top from bottom.
scenes.narration: Three planes name the sections: sagittal, coronal and horizontal.

scenes.tts: A horizontal cut runs along the forebrain's axis. How does it pass through the brainstem?
scenes.visual: A horizontal plane slices the head. The forebrain axis lies in the plane; a question mark sits at the brainstem.
scenes.narration: A horizontal cut runs along the forebrain's axis. How does it pass through the brainstem?

scenes.tts: Roughly across it, because the brainstem's axis runs up and down.
scenes.visual: The plane crosses the brainstem almost at right angles. Label: roughly transverse.
scenes.narration: Roughly across it, because the brainstem's axis runs up and down.

scenes.tts: So the tube tells you where things are. What each place does is another question.
scenes.visual: The labelled tube and adult brain side by side. On-screen takeaway: the tube tells you where, not what.
scenes.narration: So the tube tells you where things are. What each place does is another question.

scenes.visual: End card: One Tube, Bent Once.
